title: Unit – 2 : Session – 3 : SLO – 2  |  Introduction to Linked Lists
sections: 1. sequence (chain/collection) — a linked list is a sequence of data elements.
2. nodes — the data elements of a linked list.
3. foundation (base/building block) — linked lists underlie stacks, queues and their variants.
4. chain (sequence) of nodes — each node holds data field(s) and a pointer to the next node.
5. self-referential structure — a node points to another node of the same type.
6. address of the first node — START stores the first node's address.
7. START — traversal begins from START, following next pointers.
8. list is empty — START = NULL means the linked list is empty.
9. data (records/elements) — efficient storage with insertion, deletion and updation at the cost of extra pointer space.
10. C implementation: struct node { int data; struct node *next; };
